title: Changes in Bioelement Contents of Honeybees Induced by Nosema Ceranae Infection
author: Aneta Ptaszynska
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.qwedxbe
materials: DNA was extracted from each of the pooled samples of homogenized worker bees as follows: 100 μl of each homogenate was added to 180 μl of lysis buffer and 20 μl of proteinase K and total DNA was isolated using the DNeasy Blood and Tissue Kit (Qiagen) according to the manufacturer’s instructions. Subsequently, each of the DNA samples was used as a template for detection of N . apis and N . ceranae 16S rDNA by PCR with Nosema -specific primers: 321-APIS for N . apis and 218-MITOC for N . ceranae [21].

Honeybee samples. The bioelement composition in each of the pooled worker bee samples was determined using Inductively Coupled Plasma Optical Emission Spectrometry (ICP-OES, iCAP Series 6500, Thermo Scientific, USA). Two sets of pooled bees (10 workers each) were mineralized in a Microwave Digestion System (Bergh of Speedwave, Eningen, Germany) by using optical, temperature and pressure monitoring of each sample during acid digestion in teflon vials (type DAP 100). The mineralized worker bee bodies were digested with 7 ml HNO 3 (65% v/v) and 3 ml H 2 O 2 (30% v/v). Each of the samples were performed in triplicate. Therefore 6 measurements were taken for each experimental colony, giving a total of 30 measurements for each bioelement (5 colonies x 2 pooled samples x 3 replicates). Honey samples. In total, 12 honey samples were analysed: four spring honey (two from NF and two from NI colonies), four summer honey (two from NF and two from NI colonies) and four winter stores (two from NF and two from NI – colonies). The mineralization of each 0.5g honey sample was conducted in a Microwave Digestion System (Bergh of Speedwave, Eningen, Germany) by using optical, temperature and pressure monitoring of each sample during acid digestion in teflon vials (type DAP 100). The mineralized honey samples were digested with 7 ml HNO 3 (65% v/v) and 3 ml H 2 O 2 (30% v/v). Each of the samples were performed in triplicate. The mineralisation of honybees and honey process was as follows: 15 mins from room temperature to 140°C, 5 mins at 140°C, 15 mins from 140°C to 185°C, 10 mins at 185°C and then cooling down to room temperature. The pressure did not exceed 20 bars during mineralisation. After the mineralisation, the clear solution was cooled to room temperature and then transferred to 50 ml graduated flasks and filled with deionized water (ELGA Pure Lab Classic). Soil samples. Six soil samples were also taken. Three were taken in the immediate vicinity of the colonies which were Nosema- free and similarly, the three from the Nosema -infected colonies. 0.5 grams of soil from each sample was digested in 8 ml of aqua regia, with 2 ml hydrofluoric acid in a high-pressure microwave digestion system (Berghof Speedwave, Eningen, Germany). Then the digested samples were made up to 50 ml with deionized water. The operating conditions of the ICP-OES equipment were as follows: RF generator power of 1150 W, RF generator frequency of 27.12 MHz, coolant gas flow rate of 16 L·min −1 , carrier gas flow rate of 0.65 L·min −1 , auxiliary gas flow rate of 0.4 L·min −1 , maximum integration time of 15 s, pump rate of 50 rpm, viewing configuration – axial, replicate – 3, flush time of 20 s. The following multi-element stock solutions from Inorganic Ventures were used to prepare standards for all the analyses described above: A) Analityk-46 for Cu, Fe, Mg, P, K, Na in 5% HNO 3 (1000 μg/mL) B) Analityk-47 for Al, As, Cd, Cr, Pb, Mn, Hg, Ni, Sc, Se, Sr, V, Zn in 10% HNO 3 (100 μg/mL) C) Analityk-83 for Ca, K, Mg, Na, P, S in 2% HNO 3 (1000 mg/L) D) Analityk prepared from single-element stock solutions for B, S, Si in 5% HNO 3 (1000 mg/L) E) CGMO1-1: Mo in H 2 O/tr. NH 4 OH (1000 μg/mL). The bioelement symbols are compliant with the standards of the International Union of Pure and Applied Chemistry (IUPAC).

steps.title: Capture and test for Nosema
steps.instruction: At the beginning of July 2015, capture 100 forager worker‑bees (Apis mellifera carnica) from each colony; remove 50 workers, dissect their abdomens, pool and homogenize in distilled water, and examine under an Olympus BX 61 light microscope for Nosema spp. spores; from the remaining 50 workers, pool 10, grind in distilled water for DNA analysis; if spores are detected, classify the colony as Nosema‑infected and count spores per worker bee with a hemocytometer, otherwise classify it as Nosema‑free.

steps.title: Select experimental colonies
steps.instruction: Choose five colonies classified as Nosema‑infected and five colonies classified as Nosema‑free to serve as the experimental colonies.

steps.title: Place colonies in separate sites
steps.instruction: Locate the ten experimental colonies in two sites 200 m apart, separated by a hedge, to minimise drifting while providing identical food resources.

steps.title: Collect summer bee pools
steps.instruction: In mid‑July 2015, collect two pooled samples of approximately 100 worker bees in the evenings from the outer combs of each experimental colony (both infected and free) for bioelement composition analysis.

steps.title: Collect overwintered bee pools
steps.instruction: At the end of March 2016, after the winter cleansing flight, repeat the collection of ~100‑bee pools from each experimental colony to assess overwintered bee bioelement composition.

steps.title: Confirm infection status of pools
steps.instruction: From each bee pool, subject 50 workers to DNA analysis and microscopy to confirm N. ceranae infection status.

steps.title: Feed colonies for overwintering
steps.instruction: In autumn, feed all colonies sugar‑water syrup at a 2:1 (sugar:water) ratio in preparation for overwintering.

steps.title: Collect soil samples
steps.instruction: Take two soil samples (each in triplicate) from the immediate vicinity of the Nosema‑free and Nosema‑infected colonies.

steps.title: Collect honey samples
steps.instruction: Harvest honey from each colony during spring (May 2015), summer (August 2015) and winter (January 2016); store each sample in sterile jars until bioelement analysis.

steps.title: Perform statistical analyses
steps.instruction: Analyze bioelement data using Tukey tests (one‑way ANOVA, α = 0.05) in Statistica v12.0, conduct principal component analysis (PCA) on log‑transformed, centred, and standardised data, and run two‑way ANOVAs for each bioelement as described.
